text:
isobel: FYI hit a weird one in our devcontainer: I installed redwoodctl with `pipx` inside a codespace container, login succeeded, but `redwoodctl localtest` run as the devcontainer user can't see the profile. Looks like pipx created a shim under /root/.local/pipx but my container user is vscode. Any ideas?

marco: pipx often writes the venvs under the invoking user's home (so if you ran pipx with sudo or as root during image build it ends up in /root). show `which redwoodctl` and `echo $HOME` from both the build and runtime contexts.

isobel:```
# during Dockerfile build
RUN pipx install redwoodctl
# at runtime
$ whoami
vscode
$ which redwoodctl
/root/.local/bin/redwoodctl
$ echo $HOME
/home/vscode
```
So the binary is owned by root and PATH points to /root/.local/bin. Running it works but it uses root's XDG paths for profiles. localtest says "no profiles found" because it checked /root/.config/redwood.

zhi: yep. installer side-effect: installing CLI as root creates config in root's $HOME. Solutions: 1) in Dockerfile, install redwoodctl as the runtime user (e.g., `RUN su vscode -c "pipx install redwoodctl"`), 2) add a wrapper that sets REDWOOD_CONFIG to /home/vscode/.config/redwood, or 3) have the CLI detect mismatched UID/HOME and prefer a resolved runtime HOME when invoked by a different user.

marco: for images, pattern we've used: put a small postinstall script that moves the venv and symlinks the binary into /usr/local/bin and ensures config is copied to /etc/redwood as a machine fallback. Example:```
# in Dockerfile
RUN pipx install redwoodctl && \n    mkdir -p /etc/redwood && \n    cp /root/.config/redwood/* /etc/redwood/ || true && \n    ln -s /root/.local/bin/redwoodctl /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl
```
Then make sure CLI checks /etc/redwood as fallback.

isobel: quick local workaround that unblocked me:```
sudo chown -R vscode:vscode /root/.local/bin/redwoodctl /root/.local/pipx && \n    mkdir -p /home/vscode/.config/redwood && \n    cp -r /root/.config/redwood/* /home/vscode/.config/redwood/ && \n    chown -R vscode:vscode /home/vscode/.config/redwood
```
After that `redwoodctl localtest` as vscode user worked.

zhi: filed GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/734 - "installer in container builds can seed root config; prefer runtime user or add machine fallback". Suggestion: CLI check order: $REDWOOD_CONFIG, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME, runtime resolved HOME (getpwuid), /etc/redwood, /var/lib/redwood. Also add a clear warning when HOME and uid don't match binary owner.

build-bot: CI note: nightly container images failing in integration job #987 due to missing profiles. Added temporary Dockerfile change to install redwoodctl as the vscode user.

marco: small UX nudge: add `redwoodctl doctor` that prints where it will look for profiles and which one is active. That would have surfaced the root-vs-user mismatch quickly.

isobel: agreed. Thanks all, workaround saved the day. Leaving a note in our devcontainer README to avoid root pipx installs. :white_check_mark:
